topic: Septic shock in children: recognition and first-hour management

slides.title: Pediatric Septic Shock: First-Hour Plan
slides.subtitle: SSC 2020 & IAP step-by-step resuscitation algorithm for MD/DNB exams

slides.title: Recognition: Don't Wait for Hypotension
slides.subtitle: Early clinical signs of compensated shock
points: **Hypotension is a late sign**; recognize tachycardia, poor perfusion & altered sensorium early.
**Warm shock**: bounding pulses, flash CRT (<1 s), warm peripheries, wide pulse pressure.
**Cold shock**: feeble pulses, CRT >2 s, mottled cool skin, narrow pulse pressure.
**Phoenix Sepsis Criteria (2024)**: >=2 organ dysfunction pts; shock = sepsis + >=1 CV point.
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Hypotension <5th centile (SBP <70+2x age yr, 1-10 yr) = decompensated.

slides.title: 0–5 Min: Airway, Breathing & Access
slides.subtitle: Immediate bedside priorities
points: Give **high-flow O2** (non-rebreather/HFNC); prepare early intubation if refractory.
Obtain **2 large-bore IVs**; if failed in 90 sec or 2 attempts, insert **IO needle**.
Draw **blood cultures** (2 sites if feasible), VBG, lactate, CBC, RFT, LFT, glucose, Ca2+.
Check **POC glucose & ionized Ca2+** immediately; correct hypoglycemia & hypocalcemia.
slides.highlight: Red flag: Avoid etomidate for RSI in septic shock (adrenal suppression risk per SSC).

slides.title: Within 1 Hour: Empiric Antibiotics
slides.subtitle: Do not delay for LP or imaging
points: Start **IV broad-spectrum antibiotics** within 1 hr of recognition (3 hr if no shock).
Community (1 mo+): **Ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IV q12h** (max 2 g/dose) + Vancomycin if MRSA risk.
Neonates: **Ampicillin** + **Gentamicin** (or Cefotaxime if meningitis suspected).
Hospital-acquired/immunocompromised: **Pip-Tazo** or **Meropenem** + Vancomycin.
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Every 1-hour delay in antibiotics significantly increases PICU mortality.

slides.title: Fluid Boluses: PICU vs No-PICU Rule
slides.subtitle: SSC 2020 balanced crystalloid protocol
points: **With PICU availability**: Give **10–20 mL/kg** balanced crystalloids (RL/Plasmalyte) IV/IO.
Reassess after **each bolus**; up to **40–60 mL/kg** in 1st hour if fluid-responsive.
**STOP fluids** immediately if hepatomegaly, basal crepitations or gallop rhythm appear.
**No PICU & no hypotension**: Avoid bolus fluids; start maintenance fluids (FEAST trial).
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Balanced crystalloids preferred over 0.9% NS (less hyperchloremic acidosis).

slides.title: Fluid-Refractory Shock: Vasopressors
slides.subtitle: Epinephrine (Cold/First-Line) || Norepinephrine (Warm Shock)
points: Preferred in **cold shock** / low CO || Preferred in **warm shock** / low SVR
Dose: **0.05–0.3 mcg/kg/min** IV/IO inf. || Dose: **0.05–0.3 mcg/kg/min** IV/IO inf.
Beta-1 + alpha-1 agonist (inotrope) || Potent alpha-1 agonist (vasoconstrictor)
Safe via **peripheral IV/IO** initially || Safe via **peripheral IV/IO** initially
slides.highlight: Red flag: Never delay vasoactives waiting for central line; dilute & run peripherally.

slides.title: Refractory Shock & 1st-Hour Targets
slides.subtitle: Escalation & resuscitation endpoints
points: Refractory shock: **Hydrocortisone** 2 mg/kg IV (max 100 mg), then 1 mg/kg IV q6h (per IAP).
Target **MAP >=5th centile** for age, **CRT <= 2 sec**, warm extremities & normal sensorium.
Target **urine output >= 1 mL/kg/hr**, normal mental status & **ScvO2 >= 70%**.
Monitor **lactate clearance** (>10% drop q2h); consider **Milrinone** if cold + normotensive.
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Rule out pneumothorax, tamponade & IAH in refractory shock.

slides.title: PG Viva & Exam High-Yield Pearls
slides.subtitle: Must-know SSC 2020 & IAP updates
points: SSC 2020 **removed** routine 60 mL/kg push in resource-limited settings without hypotension.
**Epinephrine or Norepinephrine** replaced Dopamine as first-line vasoactive in pediatrics.
Correct **hypoglycemia** (D10W 2–5 mL/kg IV) & **hypocalcemia** (Ca gluc 10% 0.5–1 mL/kg IV).
slides.highlight: Remember: 1st-hour goal = O2 + IV/IO + Abx + Titrated Fluids + Early Vasoactives!

caption:
Every minute in the first hour of pediatric septic shock decides survival—and your PICU viva score. 🚨

Here is the complete first-hour resuscitation algorithm updated for MD/DNB exams:
• Early recognition (before hypotension sets in) + Phoenix 2024 criteria
• 0–5 min airway, IO access & point-of-care metabolic checks
• SSC 2020 fluid rules: PICU vs resource-limited settings (FEAST trial impact)
• First-line vasoactives, peripheral administration & refractory shock escalation

Which vasoactive do you reach for first in your PICU—Epinephrine or Norepinephrine? Drop it below! 👇

Save 🔖 & share with a batchmate

For education only; follow local protocols.
